moments.application: Take a recent task and rewrite it as a verifiable result.
moments.check_question: What fact would prove that you moved forward? Name your definition of done.
moments.micro_practice: Rewrite one activity as result, action and evidence.
moments.takeaway: Being busy is not the same as progressing.
moments.handoff: Carry the result into the interruption diagnosis.

moments.explanation: Reaction without a rule fragments the week and displaces chosen results. Observe which personal reaction you can change.
key_points: Separate real urgency from perceived pressure.
Record each context switch before explaining it.
moments.application: Review two interruptions and classify them as handle, batch, delegate or defer.
moments.check_question: Which interruption changed a justified priority? Separate external pressure from your response.
moments.micro_practice: Set one default response for a recurring interruption.
moments.takeaway: Reaction needs a rule, not blame.
moments.handoff: Use the record to identify value-creating work.

moments.explanation: Task volume does not show value; a result must serve a stated purpose. Classify from the purpose you chose for your week.
key_points: Separate value creation, maintenance, coordination and noise.
Do not erase necessary maintenance: expose its cost.
moments.application: Classify five recent activities and justify one uncertain category.
moments.check_question: Which activity consumes time without supporting a necessary result? Mark the category that remains uncertain.
moments.micro_practice: Place one ambiguous activity on the map and note the missing evidence.
moments.takeaway: Value is argued, not assumed.
moments.handoff: Turn the map into a weekly intention.

moments.explanation: A concrete intention comes before effort: define what must change and for whom. Write an intention compatible with your real boundaries.
key_points: Write a result with a definition of done.
State the boundary that prevents uncontrolled expansion.
moments.application: Complete: “By week end ___ will be ready, proven by ___.”
moments.check_question: Does the statement help decide what stays out? State the boundary you will not negotiate.
moments.micro_practice: Write one priority in a sentence and remove vague verbs.
moments.takeaway: Direction comes before intensity.
moments.handoff: Test the intention against the real week map.

moments.explanation: A week map turns scattered recollection into a reviewable record. Use only personal records you can review.
key_points: Include meetings, tasks, blocks and context switches.
Describe facts before judging them.
moments.application: Reconstruct one day in blocks and mark each block’s output.
moments.check_question: Which period cannot be explained with sufficient evidence? Acknowledge any gap in your record.
moments.micro_practice: Complete a morning, afternoon and close record for one real day.
moments.takeaway: Observe before redesigning.
moments.handoff: Use the map to select only three priorities.

moments.explanation: Three priorities force comparison and make trade-offs visible. Explicitly accept the work you will leave for later.
key_points: Justify each priority with purpose and evidence.
Record what is deferred and why.
moments.application: Rank five candidate results and keep only three.
moments.check_question: Which priority would move if a verified urgency appeared? Expose your main trade-off.
moments.micro_practice: Write three priorities and one explicit trade-off for each.
moments.takeaway: Prioritizing also means deciding what not to do now.
moments.handoff: Test the three priorities with shared criteria.

moments.explanation: An explicit matrix reduces decisions based only on pressure or preference. Choose which uncertainty you can accept without delegating judgment.
key_points: Compare impact, real urgency, effort, dependency and risk.
Explain ties and missing data.
moments.application: Score two results with the same criteria and state the trade-off.
moments.check_question: What missing fact could reverse the order? State the uncertainty you will accept.
moments.micro_practice: Review one priority against five criteria and mark one uncertainty.
moments.takeaway: Visible criteria make a decision reviewable.
moments.handoff: Turn the chosen priority into a protected block.

moments.explanation: A priority without reserved time loses to immediate work. Reserve time without invading non-negotiable personal commitments.
key_points: Each block needs purpose, output and a definition of done.
Keep space for real coordination and contingencies.
moments.application: Design a 45–90 minute block with input, output and boundary.
moments.check_question: What must be ready before the block starts? Confirm the block fits your week.
moments.micro_practice: Schedule a real block and record one valid cancellation condition.
moments.takeaway: The calendar makes a priority executable.
moments.handoff: Define how you will defend the block.

moments.explanation: Protecting focus requires agreed responses to predictable interruptions. Define a response that respects your real responsibilities.
key_points: Choose what to handle, delegate, batch, defer or discard.
Make legitimate exceptions explicit.
moments.application: Write one rule for messages, urgent requests and context changes.
moments.check_question: Who may trigger an exception, and with what evidence? Clarify the exception you would handle.
moments.micro_practice: Rehearse a short response that protects a block without ignoring real urgency.
moments.takeaway: A useful boundary includes an exception path.
moments.handoff: Test the rule for a week and record what happens.

moments.explanation: Review compares plan and facts; it does not reward or punish the feeling of effort. Evaluate your decision with facts from the observed period.
key_points: Record results, completed blocks and deviations.
Keep one useful rule and change one concrete friction.
moments.application: Compare one planned priority with its evidence and choose keep, adjust or remove.
moments.check_question: Is the explanation factual or merely convenient? Separate the fact from your interpretation.
moments.micro_practice: Write one learning, one decision and the evidence behind both.
moments.takeaway: Review turns experience into a testable rule.
moments.handoff: Integrate the findings into a visible board.

moments.explanation: The weekly system puts decisions and evidence in one view for action and review. Keep only information that helps you decide.
key_points: Show priorities, blocks, status and next decision.
Keep the system small and current.
moments.application: Create a one-page view with three priorities and their next evidence.
moments.check_question: Can the state be understood without reconstructing conversations? Choose the next decision you will show.
moments.micro_practice: Remove one field that changes no decision and add the missing fact.
moments.takeaway: Visibility should serve the next decision.
moments.handoff: Repeat the cycle with one improved rule.

orientation.title: Your week as evidence
orientation.body: Use your own records to choose three results, protect blocks and adjust one rule without demanding perfection.
orientation.use_case: One real week of work or study.
orientation.ready_when: You have a calendar, tasks and personal authority to test a change.

preparation_prompts.title: Observable period
preparation_prompts.purpose: Bound the period and its records.
preparation_prompts.prompt: Which seven days can you reconstruct from records? State what depends on you and your boundary.

preparation_prompts.title: Guiding result
preparation_prompts.purpose: State the result that will guide classification.
preparation_prompts.prompt: Which concrete result should be closer to done? State what depends on you and your boundary.

preparation_prompts.title: Boundaries and permissions
preparation_prompts.prompt: Which data, commitment or boundary can you not change? State what depends on you and your boundary.

steps.title: Week inventory
steps.brief: Build a baseline before changing the system. Use your own week and a boundary you can sustain.
actions: Record blocks, context switches and outputs.
Define which record you can maintain without external help.
steps.deliverable: One real-week log for your review
steps.example: Synthetic personal example: Monday 9:00–10:00 meeting; output: decision still pending.
criteria: Covers at least five days or the available period.
steps.watch_out: Do not reconstruct the week from memory when records exist. Do not label care or personal duties as “noise”.
steps.reflection: Which part of the week is still invisible? What will you choose to do differently?
steps.next_connection: Classify the work by value type.

steps.title: Value map
steps.brief: Separate useful work, support, coordination and reaction. Use your own week and a boundary you can sustain.
actions: Label each block with one category.
Mark uncertainty where context is missing.
Mark one category you would change with new evidence.
steps.deliverable: Activity value map with your stated criterion
steps.example: Synthetic personal example: Prepare delivery = value; coordinate access = necessary support.
steps.watch_out: Do not call all non-delivery work noise. Do not label care or personal duties as “noise”.
steps.reflection: Which category takes more space than expected? What will you choose to do differently?
steps.next_connection: Use the map to locate attention leaks.

steps.title: Main frictions
steps.brief: Select the two frictions that most alter results. Use your own week and a boundary you can sustain.
actions: Choose one friction under your direct control.
steps.deliverable: Two evidence-backed frictions under your control
steps.example: Synthetic personal example: Unruled messages: four context switches and one moved delivery.
criteria: Avoid assigning motives to other people.
steps.watch_out: Temporal association does not prove causation. Do not label care or personal duties as “noise”.
steps.reflection: Which friction can you change without external authority? What will you choose to do differently?
steps.next_connection: Turn the diagnosis into three results.

routes.title: Practise decisions
routes.brief: Turn criteria into priorities and blocks.

steps.title: Weekly results
steps.brief: Write three bounded, verifiable results. Use your own week and a boundary you can sustain.
actions: Declare what is out of scope.
State the trade-off you are willing to sustain.
steps.deliverable: Three candidate results for your week
steps.example: Synthetic personal example: Deliver a reviewable draft with five cited sources.
steps.watch_out: Do not use “work on” or “make progress” as the finish condition. Do not label care or personal duties as “noise”.
steps.reflection: Which result serves the immediate purpose most? What will you choose to do differently?
steps.next_connection: Compare the results with shared criteria.

steps.title: Priority test
steps.brief: Rank results with explicit criteria. Use your own week and a boundary you can sustain.
actions: Compare impact, real urgency and effort.
Add dependency, risk and missing data.
Choose which uncertainty you will accept before acting.
steps.deliverable: Priority matrix with your boundaries
steps.example: Synthetic personal example: Result A: high impact, dependency cleared, medium risk.
criteria: The same criteria apply to all results.
steps.watch_out: Do not treat a score as an automatic truth. Do not label care or personal duties as “noise”.
steps.reflection: What fact could change the order? What will you choose to do differently?
steps.next_connection: Reserve time for the selected priorities.

steps.title: Protected calendar
steps.brief: Turn priorities into executable blocks. Use your own week and a boundary you can sustain.
actions: Reserve blocks with purpose and output.
Add preparation and definition of done.
Reserve a block compatible with your real commitments.
steps.deliverable: Protected weekly calendar compatible with your commitments
steps.example: Synthetic personal example: Tuesday 9:00–10:30: draft; output: reviewable version.
steps.watch_out: Do not fill every free slot or ignore fixed commitments. Do not label care or personal duties as “noise”.
steps.reflection: Which block needs prior preparation? What will you choose to do differently?
steps.next_connection: Define the interruption response.

routes.title: Transfer one rule
routes.brief: Compare facts and design the next cycle.

steps.title: Execution record
steps.brief: Compare the plan with what happened. Use your own week and a boundary you can sustain.
actions: Mark blocks completed, moved or cancelled.
Personally mark each output as achieved or pending.
steps.deliverable: Plan-versus-execution record for personal use
steps.example: Synthetic personal example: Block completed; partial output; one source still needs review.
steps.watch_out: Do not confuse attendance in a block with a completed result. Do not label care or personal duties as “noise”.
steps.reflection: What decision became possible because of the record? What will you choose to do differently?
steps.next_connection: Explain one deviation without automatic justification.

steps.title: Deviation analysis
steps.brief: Explain one difference between plan and facts. Use your own week and a boundary you can sustain.
actions: Separate personal control from external dependency.
Separate the response you could personally change.
steps.deliverable: Deviation note with one chosen response
steps.example: Synthetic personal example: The block started late because input was not ready; prepare it the day before.
criteria: The action addresses the observed condition.
steps.watch_out: Do not turn one case into a universal rule. Do not label care or personal duties as “noise”.
steps.reflection: What alternative was under your control? What will you choose to do differently?
steps.next_connection: Choose one rule to keep and one to adjust.

steps.title: Rule for next week
steps.brief: Turn review into a testable adjustment. Use your own week and a boundary you can sustain.
actions: Change one friction and schedule review.
Choose the personal rule you will test for one more week.
steps.deliverable: Reviewable weekly rule for the next cycle
steps.example: Synthetic personal example: Prepare inputs the day before; review on Friday.
criteria: The rule is concrete and bounded.
A review date and evidence are defined.
steps.watch_out: Do not change many rules at once if that hides what helped. Do not label care or personal duties as “noise”.
steps.reflection: What evidence will keep or remove the rule? What will you choose to do differently?
steps.next_connection: Add the rule to the visible system.

rubric.label: Initial
rubric.description: A partial record exists, but criteria or evidence are missing.

rubric.label: Applicable
rubric.description: Priorities, blocks and review connect to evidence.

rubric.label: Transferable
rubric.description: The rule repeats, is reviewed and keeps clear boundaries.

transfer_challenge.title: Test one rule for another week
transfer_challenge.brief: Repeat the cycle without changing many conditions at once.
actions: Choose one rule under your control.
transfer_challenge.evidence: Two comparable weeks and one documented decision.
transfer_challenge.review_after: At the end of the next week.

chapters.explanation: Productivity means completing results that serve an explicit purpose. Apply it to your week and keep your personal boundary.
chapters.decision: Define the result first, then decide which activity deserves space. You decide and review against your records.
actions: Write purpose and definition of done.
Remove one activity that changes no decision.
chapters.rule: No task becomes a priority without a result and evidence. Do not sacrifice non-negotiable personal duties.
chapters.example: Synthetic personal example: Replace “answer email” with “resolve the three decisions blocking delivery”.
chapters.antipattern: Using task count as proof of productivity.
chapters.expected_evidence: A defensible priority decision. The individual keeps it in the review.
chapters.limit: Necessary maintenance may remain; its cost must stay visible. It does not replace agreements with others.

chapters.explanation: A time log reduces dependence on vague recollection of the week. Apply it to your week and keep your personal boundary.
chapters.decision: Record facts for a sufficient period before redesigning. You decide and review against your records.
chapters.rule: A conclusion requires an inspectable record. Do not sacrifice non-negotiable personal duties.
chapters.example: Synthetic personal example: Record “10:00–10:35, meeting, output: date agreed”.
chapters.antipattern: Backfilling the log to confirm a prior impression.
chapters.expected_evidence: Traceable time log. The individual keeps it in the review.
chapters.limit: The log describes the observed period, not a universal rule. It does not replace agreements with others.

chapters.explanation: The value map separates creation, support, coordination and reaction. Apply it to your week and keep your personal boundary.
chapters.decision: Keep necessary work and question work that supports no result. You decide and review against your records.
actions: Total time only to describe, not promise impact.
chapters.rule: A category without a reason remains provisional. Do not sacrifice non-negotiable personal duties.
chapters.example: Synthetic personal example: Coordinating access is necessary support when it enables delivery.
chapters.antipattern: Calling necessary but less visible obligations “noise”.
chapters.expected_evidence: Reviewable value map. The individual keeps it in the review.
chapters.limit: Classification depends on purpose and may change with context. It does not replace agreements with others.

chapters.explanation: The matrix exposes impact, real urgency, effort, dependency and risk. Apply it to your week and keep your personal boundary.
chapters.decision: Rank results with the same criteria and explain the trade-off. You decide and review against your records.
chapters.rule: Scoring informs; the accountable person decides. Do not sacrifice non-negotiable personal duties.
chapters.example: Synthetic personal example: Two results tie: choose the one that clears a critical dependency.
chapters.antipattern: Adding scores without explaining meaning or uncertainty.
chapters.expected_evidence: Three justified priorities. The individual keeps it in the review.
chapters.limit: A matrix does not replace judgment, rights or existing commitments. It does not replace agreements with others.

chapters.explanation: A work limit exposes what is active and what is waiting. Apply it to your week and keep your personal boundary.
chapters.decision: Finish, pause or remove before opening another front. You decide and review against your records.
chapters.rule: Every active front has a next action or is paused. Do not sacrifice non-negotiable personal duties.
chapters.example: Synthetic personal example: Keep three weekly results active and an explicit queue.
chapters.antipattern: Treating every request as started work.
chapters.expected_evidence: Fewer simultaneous fronts with clear status. The individual keeps it in the review.
chapters.limit: The appropriate limit is contextual; no automatic outcome is promised. It does not replace agreements with others.

chapters.explanation: A protected block links priority, time and a concrete output. Apply it to your week and keep your personal boundary.
chapters.decision: Schedule only when inputs and a definition of done exist. You decide and review against your records.
chapters.rule: Redesign a block with no output before it starts. Do not sacrifice non-negotiable personal duties.
chapters.example: Synthetic personal example: 09:00–10:30, produce a reviewable draft with five sources ready.
chapters.antipattern: Filling the calendar without coordination or contingency capacity.
chapters.expected_evidence: Executable block. The individual keeps it in the review.
chapters.limit: A legitimate, documented exception may reschedule a block. It does not replace agreements with others.

chapters.explanation: The protocol avoids deciding every interruption from scratch. Apply it to your week and keep your personal boundary.
chapters.decision: Choose what to handle, delegate, batch, defer or discard. You decide and review against your records.
chapters.rule: Every exception records reason and next decision. Do not sacrifice non-negotiable personal duties.
chapters.example: Synthetic personal example: Non-urgent messages are batched; critical incidents use the agreed channel.
chapters.antipattern: Blocking requests without a valid urgency path.
chapters.expected_evidence: Focus protection rules. The individual keeps it in the review.
chapters.limit: The protocol does not remove surprises or replace response to real risks. It does not replace agreements with others.

chapters.explanation: Weekly review connects results, deviations and adjustments. Apply it to your week and keep your personal boundary.
chapters.decision: Keep one useful rule and change one friction per cycle. You decide and review against your records.
chapters.rule: Keep an improvement only while its evidence remains visible. Do not sacrifice non-negotiable personal duties.
chapters.example: Synthetic personal example: Keep prior preparation; adjust message rule; review Friday.
chapters.antipattern: Turning review into blame or impressions.
chapters.expected_evidence: Testable weekly rule. The individual keeps it in the review.
chapters.limit: One period is insufficient to claim general improvement. It does not replace agreements with others.

chapters.explanation: The board combines priorities, blocks, status, evidence and next action. Apply it to your week and keep your personal boundary.
chapters.decision: Show only information that changes a decision. You decide and review against your records.
chapters.rule: The board must be understandable without reconstructing conversations. Do not sacrifice non-negotiable personal duties.
chapters.example: Synthetic personal example: Priority A: active; evidence: draft; next: review Thursday.
chapters.antipattern: Building an ornamental board that costs more upkeep than the work.
chapters.expected_evidence: Visible weekly system. The individual keeps it in the review.
chapters.limit: Visibility must respect sensitive data and access rights. It does not replace agreements with others.

glossary.definition: Observable change or delivery with a definition of done.
Result chosen over explicit alternatives.
Reserved time with purpose, output and boundary.
External condition or contribution needed to continue.
Observable record used to review a claim.

faq.question: Always three priorities?
faq.answer: It is a practice limit that forces comparison; adjust it when context requires and document why. Adjust the limit using your records.

faq.question: What about a real urgency?
faq.answer: Use the defined exception, record its evidence and explicitly reschedule or remove work. Keep the commitment you can sustain.

faq.question: How do I know it improved?
faq.answer: Compare equivalent records and decide on one rule; do not turn one week into a general promise. Decide only about the observed period.

faq.question: May I share the board?
faq.answer: Only with the rights and detail level agreed for the people involved. Protect your personal information as well.

closing_checklist: Three results and trade-offs are visible.
Your blocks include purpose and output.
Your boundary and exception are written.
The review ends in a decision.

graph_summary.title: From diagnosis to review
graph_summary.body: The prompts turn your records into a map, priorities, calendar, protocol and review; each output can be checked before continuing.
graph_summary.independent_use: Each prompt can run alone when you provide its declared input artifact; it never invents a prior output.

items.purpose: Turn scattered records into a factual map of the week. Apply the decision to your own practice.
items.when: When you need a baseline before changing the calendar. Use records you can review.
workflow: Gather available calendar, task and note records.
Order activities by day, duration and output.
Summarize patterns as observations, not causes.
Close the diagnosis with the period you can actually observe.
guardrails: Do not invent periods or outputs.
Declare any reconstruction from memory.
Do not fill record gaps with an imagined week.
acceptance_criteria: Every block has a source or a marker.
The summary separates facts from inference.
At least one relevant gap is identified.
The map identifies which records you can verify yourself.
edge_cases: Incomplete records: deliver a partial map.
Overlapping activities: keep both and mark conflict.
items.tradeoff: More detail improves traceability but increases recording effort. Autonomy preserves context but requires honest self-review.
items.demo_artifact: Personal Monday-to-Friday record: 14 h of meetings, 11 h of focused work, 6 h of messages, and 4 h of administration. The proposal is due Friday; two blocks have no verifiable output, and three interruptions were marked urgent without a stated consequence.
limits: Describe the observed period; do not predict performance.
It does not delegate personal decisions to AI.

items.purpose: Classify activities by their relationship to value. Apply the decision to your own practice.
items.when: When the time map exists and you must decide what to question. Use records you can review.
workflow: Read the period purpose and results.
Classify creation, maintenance, coordination or reaction.
Personally choose which activity to keep, reduce or review.
guardrails: Do not trivialize necessary maintenance.
Do not assign value without a stated purpose.
Do not classify necessary personal duties as waste.
acceptance_criteria: Every activity has a category and reason.
Uncertain cases preserve missing evidence.
The map supports keep, reduce or review decisions.
The final decision states which classification you will personally review.
edge_cases: One activity serves two categories: record primary and secondary.
If a constraint cannot move, adapt the plan instead of hiding it.
items.tradeoff: A simple taxonomy aids decisions but loses nuance; preserve exceptions. Autonomy preserves context but requires honest self-review.
items.demo_artifact: Factual map: 35 h recorded; proposal 6 h and one draft; meetings 14 h and three decisions; messages 6 h with no deliverable; administration 4 h; 5 h unrecorded. Expected weekly outcome: proposal reviewed on Thursday.
limits: Classification is contextual, not universal.
It does not delegate personal decisions to AI.

items.purpose: Choose three results and expose trade-offs. Apply the decision to your own practice.
items.when: When candidate results exceed available capacity. Use records you can review.
workflow: Compare purpose, impact and real urgency.
State the weekly trade-off you can sustain.
guardrails: Do not use pressure as the only criterion.
Expose data that could change the order.
Do not accept a priority that conflicts with a non-negotiable boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Three observable results.
Each has a rationale and trade-off.
No hidden tie remains.
Every priority fits within a stated personal boundary.
edge_cases: Everything seems urgent: request evidence of date and consequence.
Capacity is missing: reduce scope before adding priority.
items.tradeoff: A limit of three creates clarity but defers legitimate work. Autonomy preserves context but requires honest self-review.
items.demo_artifact: Activity classification: proposal = creation; scope meeting = coordination; daily status = maintenance; reactive messages = reaction. Two meetings produced no decision. Candidate outcomes: reviewed proposal, budget decision, and closure of one critical source.
limits: It does not guarantee completion; it creates a reviewable decision.
It does not delegate personal decisions to AI.

items.purpose: Test priorities against dependencies, effort, risk and calendar reality. Apply the decision to your own practice.
items.when: Before reserving blocks or committing a date. Use records you can review.
workflow: Compare effort with declared available space.
Decide which risk you will accept and which needs external help.
guardrails: Do not invent availability or agreements.
Separate internal from external dependency.
Do not assume personal control over an external dependency.
acceptance_criteria: Every risk has a signal and response.
Dependencies have status.
The final decision explains the trade-off.
The recommendation separates your action from required help.
edge_cases: Dependency has no owner: mark blocked.
Risk lacks evidence: treat as hypothesis.
items.tradeoff: More validation reduces surprise but consumes time before execution. Autonomy preserves context but requires honest self-review.
items.demo_artifact: Three prioritized outcomes: proposal approved Thursday; budget decision Friday; source rights confirmed Wednesday. Real capacity: 10 h. Reviewer available Thursday at 15:00. Supplier dependency still unconfirmed. Boundary: no work after 18:00.
limits: This is a reality test, not certainty about the future.
It does not delegate personal decisions to AI.

items.purpose: Turn priorities into blocks with output and boundary. Apply the decision to your own practice.
items.when: When priorities have passed the reality test. Use records you can review.
workflow: Assign blocks using declared work and available energy.
Define input, output and definition of done.
Close with a calendar compatible with your real commitments.
guardrails: Do not fill all capacity.
Do not move fixed commitments without authorization.
Do not reserve capacity already committed elsewhere.
acceptance_criteria: Every priority has a block.
Every block has an output.
Conflicts are marked.
The calendar’s next action is under your control.
edge_cases: No block is large enough: split the output.
Dependency pending: schedule preparation, not execution.
items.tradeoff: Long blocks reduce switching but reduce flexibility for exceptions. Autonomy preserves context but requires honest self-review.
items.demo_artifact: Reality test: keep proposal scope at version 1; reduce the budget memo to one page; defer dashboard polish. Estimate: 3 h for inputs and 2 h for review. Risk: reviewer availability. Mitigation: send the draft Wednesday at noon.
limits: The calendar is an executable hypothesis and must be reviewed.
It does not delegate personal decisions to AI.

items.purpose: Define default responses for interruptions. Apply the decision to your own practice. Apply the protocol for one practice week and keep the record that prompt-07 will review.
items.when: When messages and requests repeatedly displace blocks. Use records you can review.
workflow: Assign handle, delegate, batch, defer or discard.
Select one personal response for each recurring interruption.
guardrails: Include a path for real urgency.
Do not block care, safety or critical service duties.
Do not use focus as an excuse to ignore legitimate urgency.
acceptance_criteria: Every type has response and timing.
Exceptions are explicit.
Language protects work without hostility.
Every proposed response respects your real responsibilities.
edge_cases: Ambiguous request: ask for consequence and date.
Authority conflict: escalate instead of improvising.
items.tradeoff: A rule protects focus but can delay coordination without exceptions. Autonomy preserves context but requires honest self-review.
items.demo_artifact: Proposed blocks: Tuesday 09:00–11:00 outline; Wednesday 09:00–12:00 draft; Thursday 10:00–11:00 verification; Thursday 15:00–16:00 review; Friday 09:00–10:00 decision. Two hours remain unassigned as reserve. Conflict: meeting Wednesday at 10:00.
limits: Adapt the protocol to context and review its effects.
It does not delegate personal decisions to AI.

items.purpose: Compare plan, execution and evidence to choose one adjustment. Apply the decision to your own practice. Use prompt-08 only when an open decision requires governed sources; otherwise close the review.
items.when: At period close or before planning the next week. Use records you can review. The sequence may end here.
workflow: Identify one useful rule and one friction.
Propose an adjustment and review date.
Choose one personal rule for the next cycle.
guardrails: Do not turn perceived effort into evidence.
Do not generalize from one period.
Do not turn perceived effort into evidence of progress.
acceptance_criteria: Facts and inferences are separate.
Each adjustment addresses a friction.
A keep-or-remove criterion exists.
The chosen adjustment has evidence you can record again.
edge_cases: Insufficient evidence: preserve the question; do not invent a conclusion.
If a constraint cannot move, adapt the plan instead of hiding it.
items.tradeoff: Testing one rule slows the pace of change but makes the evidence easier to connect to that adjustment. Autonomy preserves context but requires honest self-review. Consulting sources adds traceability but is not required when local evidence is enough to close the decision.
items.demo_artifact: Protocol applied for one week: batch messages at 12:00 and 16:00; urgent only for safety or a deadline under 4 h. Log: 11 interruptions, 6 queued, 3 handled, and 2 escalated. The proposal was delivered Thursday; one response missed its agreed deadline.
limits: Review supports decisions; it does not prove general improvement.
It does not delegate personal decisions to AI.

items.purpose: Build a cited synthesis for one concrete decision. Apply the decision to your own practice.
items.when: In NotebookLM Sources, when a priority depends on governed information. Use records you can review.
guardrails: Stop when relevant sources are absent.
Do not present editorial synthesis as observed fact.
Do not use a source to decide beyond its stated scope.
acceptance_criteria: Every verifiable claim has a citation.
Disagreements remain visible.
The recommendation states its limit.
The synthesis exposes the decision that still belongs to you.
edge_cases: Sources conflict: do not force consensus.
Unclear rights: exclude the source and record the gap.
items.tradeoff: Citations improve traceability but may leave an immediate decision unanswered. Autonomy preserves context but requires honest self-review.
items.demo_artifact: Weekly review: proposal completed, budget decision partial, and source rights still unconfirmed. Chosen adjustment: protect Wednesday's drafting block. Open decision: evaluate the practice by time released or quality. Available sources: brief v2, weekly log, and official guide; none establishes causality.
limits: Use only governed sources available in the notebook.
It does not delegate personal decisions to AI.

phases.label: Diagnose
phases.purpose: Agree what activity creates progress and who reviews the evidence.

phases.label: Design
phases.purpose: Assign priorities, owners, dependencies and compatible blocks.

phases.label: Sustain
phases.purpose: Govern exceptions, review, rights and adoption of the system.

moments.explanation: Activity describes movement; progress requires a useful completed result. The team agrees the result and who will check the output.
key_points: Name the result before listing tasks.
Use observable evidence to recognize progress.
moments.application: Take a recent task and rewrite it as a verifiable result.
moments.check_question: What fact would prove that you moved forward? State who will review the evidence.
moments.micro_practice: Rewrite one activity as result, action and evidence.
moments.takeaway: Being busy is not the same as progressing.
moments.handoff: Carry the result into the interruption diagnosis.

moments.explanation: Reaction without a rule fragments the week and displaces chosen results. The interruption response preserves an exception authority.
key_points: Separate real urgency from perceived pressure.
Record each context switch before explaining it.
moments.application: Review two interruptions and classify them as handle, batch, delegate or defer.
moments.check_question: Which interruption changed a justified priority? Name the authority for an exception.
moments.micro_practice: Set one default response for a recurring interruption.
moments.takeaway: Reaction needs a rule, not blame.
moments.handoff: Use the record to identify value-creating work.

moments.explanation: Task volume does not show value; a result must serve a stated purpose. Affected areas review how their work is classified.
key_points: Separate value creation, maintenance, coordination and noise.
Do not erase necessary maintenance: expose its cost.
moments.application: Classify five recent activities and justify one uncertain category.
moments.check_question: Which activity consumes time without supporting a necessary result? Confirm which area must validate the category.
moments.micro_practice: Place one ambiguous activity on the map and note the missing evidence.
moments.takeaway: Value is argued, not assumed.
moments.handoff: Turn the map into a weekly intention.

moments.explanation: A concrete intention comes before effort: define what must change and for whom. The sponsor confirms purpose before asking for more effort.
key_points: Write a result with a definition of done.
State the boundary that prevents uncontrolled expansion.
moments.application: Complete: “By week end ___ will be ready, proven by ___.”
moments.check_question: Does the statement help decide what stays out? State who approves the scope.
moments.micro_practice: Write one priority in a sentence and remove vague verbs.
moments.takeaway: Direction comes before intensity.
moments.handoff: Test the intention against the real week map.

moments.explanation: A week map turns scattered recollection into a reviewable record. The shared record respects agreed permissions and custody.
key_points: Include meetings, tasks, blocks and context switches.
Describe facts before judging them.
moments.application: Reconstruct one day in blocks and mark each block’s output.
moments.check_question: Which period cannot be explained with sufficient evidence? Check record custody and permissions.
moments.micro_practice: Complete a morning, afternoon and close record for one real day.
moments.takeaway: Observe before redesigning.
moments.handoff: Use the map to select only three priorities.

moments.explanation: Three priorities force comparison and make trade-offs visible. Each result keeps an accountable person and accepted trade-off.
key_points: Justify each priority with purpose and evidence.
Record what is deferred and why.
moments.application: Rank five candidate results and keep only three.
moments.check_question: Which priority would move if a verified urgency appeared? State the trade-off accepted by the sponsor.
moments.micro_practice: Write three priorities and one explicit trade-off for each.
moments.takeaway: Prioritizing also means deciding what not to do now.
moments.handoff: Test the three priorities with shared criteria.

moments.explanation: An explicit matrix reduces decisions based only on pressure or preference. Dependencies are validated with those able to resolve them.
key_points: Compare impact, real urgency, effort, dependency and risk.
Explain ties and missing data.
moments.application: Score two results with the same criteria and state the trade-off.
moments.check_question: What missing fact could reverse the order? Identify the dependency that could change the order.
moments.micro_practice: Review one priority against five criteria and mark one uncertainty.
moments.takeaway: Visible criteria make a decision reviewable.
moments.handoff: Turn the chosen priority into a protected block.

moments.explanation: A priority without reserved time loses to immediate work. Each block coordinates accountability, inputs and output review.
key_points: Each block needs purpose, output and a definition of done.
Keep space for real coordination and contingencies.
moments.application: Design a 45–90 minute block with input, output and boundary.
moments.check_question: What must be ready before the block starts? Confirm who reviews the block output.
moments.micro_practice: Schedule a real block and record one valid cancellation condition.
moments.takeaway: The calendar makes a priority executable.
moments.handoff: Define how you will defend the block.

moments.explanation: Protecting focus requires agreed responses to predictable interruptions. Critical channels keep an agreed escalation path.
key_points: Choose what to handle, delegate, batch, defer or discard.
Make legitimate exceptions explicit.
moments.application: Write one rule for messages, urgent requests and context changes.
moments.check_question: Who may trigger an exception, and with what evidence? Define the channel for legitimate urgency.
moments.micro_practice: Rehearse a short response that protects a block without ignoring real urgency.
moments.takeaway: A useful boundary includes an exception path.
moments.handoff: Test the rule for a week and record what happens.

moments.explanation: Review compares plan and facts; it does not reward or punish the feeling of effort. The review ends in a documented adoption decision.
key_points: Record results, completed blocks and deviations.
Keep one useful rule and change one concrete friction.
moments.application: Compare one planned priority with its evidence and choose keep, adjust or remove.
moments.check_question: Is the explanation factual or merely convenient? Name the decision that belongs to the sponsor.
moments.micro_practice: Write one learning, one decision and the evidence behind both.
moments.takeaway: Review turns experience into a testable rule.
moments.handoff: Integrate the findings into a visible board.

moments.explanation: The weekly system puts decisions and evidence in one view for action and review. The board shows only authorized, necessary data.
key_points: Show priorities, blocks, status and next decision.
Keep the system small and current.
moments.application: Create a one-page view with three priorities and their next evidence.
moments.check_question: Can the state be understood without reconstructing conversations? Review the right to access status.
moments.micro_practice: Remove one field that changes no decision and add the missing fact.
moments.takeaway: Visibility should serve the next decision.
moments.handoff: Repeat the cycle with one improved rule.

orientation.title: The team week as a system
orientation.body: Align priorities, owners, reviewers, dependencies and rights before testing a shared rule.
orientation.use_case: A team with real deliveries and coordination.
orientation.ready_when: A sponsor, exercise owner and permission to review agreed records exist.

preparation_prompts.title: Observable period
preparation_prompts.purpose: Bound the period and its records.
preparation_prompts.prompt: Which seven days can you reconstruct from records? State custodian, permissions and authorized period.

preparation_prompts.title: Guiding result
preparation_prompts.purpose: State the result that will guide classification.
preparation_prompts.prompt: Which concrete result should be closer to done? State who owns the result and who will accept the evidence.

preparation_prompts.title: Boundaries and permissions
preparation_prompts.prompt: Which data, commitment or boundary can you not change? State dependency, exception and authority to resolve them.

steps.title: Week inventory
steps.brief: Build a baseline before changing the system. Bound shared records and their custody.
actions: Record blocks, context switches and outputs.
Name the record custodian and people with access.
steps.deliverable: One real-week log for the team with ownership
steps.example: Synthetic team example: Monday 9:00–10:00 meeting; output: decision still pending.
criteria: Covers at least five days or the available period.
Record custodian and permissions are documented.
steps.watch_out: Do not reconstruct the week from memory when records exist. Do not expose data or calendars without access rights.
steps.reflection: Which part of the week is still invisible? Which dependency or exception will affect adoption?
steps.next_connection: Classify the work by value type.

steps.title: Value map
steps.brief: Separate useful work, support, coordination and reaction. Align classification with affected areas.
actions: Label each block with one category.
Mark uncertainty where context is missing.
Assign a reviewer for disputed categories.
steps.deliverable: Activity value map for the team with ownership
steps.example: Synthetic team example: Prepare delivery = value; coordinate access = necessary support.
criteria: Disputed categories have a reviewer and pending decision.
steps.watch_out: Do not call all non-delivery work noise. Do not expose data or calendars without access rights.
steps.reflection: Which category takes more space than expected? Which dependency or exception will affect adoption?
steps.next_connection: Use the map to locate attention leaks.

steps.title: Main frictions
steps.brief: Select the two frictions that most alter results. Turn observed frictions into concrete responsibilities.
actions: Name the owner of each friction and related dependency.
steps.deliverable: Two evidence-backed frictions for the team with ownership
steps.example: Synthetic team example: Unruled messages: four context switches and one moved delivery.
criteria: Avoid assigning motives to other people.
Each friction has an owner and identified dependency.
steps.watch_out: Temporal association does not prove causation. Do not expose data or calendars without access rights.
steps.reflection: Which friction can you change without external authority? Which dependency or exception will affect adoption?
steps.next_connection: Turn the diagnosis into three results.

steps.title: Weekly results
steps.brief: Write three bounded, verifiable results. Write results the sponsor can accept.
actions: Declare what is out of scope.
Assign the result owner and agreed backup.
steps.deliverable: Three candidate results for the team with ownership
steps.example: Synthetic team example: Deliver a reviewable draft with five cited sources.
criteria: Each result has an accepted owner and backup.
steps.watch_out: Do not use “work on” or “make progress” as the finish condition. Do not expose data or calendars without access rights.
steps.reflection: Which result serves the immediate purpose most? Which dependency or exception will affect adoption?
steps.next_connection: Compare the results with shared criteria.

steps.title: Priority test
steps.brief: Rank results with explicit criteria. Validate the order with those managing dependencies.
actions: Compare impact, real urgency and effort.
Add dependency, risk and missing data.
Validate dependencies and risk with those able to resolve them.
steps.deliverable: Priority matrix for the team with ownership
steps.example: Synthetic team example: Result A: high impact, dependency cleared, medium risk.
criteria: The same criteria apply to all results.
Risks have a reviewer and escalation path.
steps.watch_out: Do not treat a score as an automatic truth. Do not expose data or calendars without access rights.
steps.reflection: What fact could change the order? Which dependency or exception will affect adoption?
steps.next_connection: Reserve time for the selected priorities.

steps.title: Protected calendar
steps.brief: Turn priorities into executable blocks. Coordinate blocks with other people’s commitments.
actions: Reserve blocks with purpose and output.
Add preparation and definition of done.
Align each block with its owner and dependent teams.
steps.deliverable: Protected weekly calendar for the team with ownership
steps.example: Synthetic team example: Tuesday 9:00–10:30: draft; output: reviewable version.
criteria: Blocks respect shared commitments and dependencies.
steps.watch_out: Do not fill every free slot or ignore fixed commitments. Do not expose data or calendars without access rights.
steps.reflection: Which block needs prior preparation? Which dependency or exception will affect adoption?
steps.next_connection: Define the interruption response.

steps.title: Execution record
steps.brief: Compare the plan with what happened. Share status without exceeding agreed permissions.
actions: Mark blocks completed, moved or cancelled.
Give status to the reviewer without exposing others’ data.
steps.deliverable: Plan-versus-execution record for the team with ownership
steps.example: Synthetic team example: Block completed; partial output; one source still needs review.
criteria: Status can be reviewed under current rights.
steps.watch_out: Do not confuse attendance in a block with a completed result. Do not expose data or calendars without access rights.
steps.reflection: What decision became possible because of the record? Which dependency or exception will affect adoption?
steps.next_connection: Explain one deviation without automatic justification.

steps.title: Deviation analysis
steps.brief: Explain one difference between plan and facts. Separate operating failures from external dependencies.
actions: Separate personal control from external dependency.
Separate the external dependency from the internal operating change.
steps.deliverable: Deviation note for the team with ownership
steps.example: Synthetic team example: The block started late because input was not ready; prepare it the day before.
criteria: The action addresses the observed condition.
The deviation separates internal owner and external dependency.
steps.watch_out: Do not turn one case into a universal rule. Do not expose data or calendars without access rights.
steps.reflection: What alternative was under your control? Which dependency or exception will affect adoption?
steps.next_connection: Choose one rule to keep and one to adjust.

steps.title: Rule for next week
steps.brief: Turn review into a testable adjustment. Prepare a rule that can be reviewed before scaling.
actions: Change one friction and schedule review.
Define sponsor, adoption gate and review date.
steps.deliverable: Reviewable weekly rule for the team with ownership
steps.example: Synthetic team example: Prepare inputs the day before; review on Friday.
criteria: The rule is concrete and bounded.
A review date and evidence are defined.
The rule has a sponsor and adoption condition.
steps.watch_out: Do not change many rules at once if that hides what helped. Do not expose data or calendars without access rights.
steps.reflection: What evidence will keep or remove the rule? Which dependency or exception will affect adoption?
steps.next_connection: Add the rule to the visible system.

rubric.label: Initial
rubric.description: The team records activity, but shared criteria, accountable roles or evidence are still missing.

rubric.label: Applicable
rubric.description: Priorities, protected blocks, accountable roles and shared review connect to evidence.

rubric.label: Transferable
rubric.description: Another team can adopt the rule because roles, exceptions and review are explicit.

transfer_challenge.title: Pilot one rule with the team for another week
transfer_challenge.brief: Repeat the cycle with one agreed change so its effect can be attributed.
actions: Name owner, reviewer and affected teams.
Confirm rights, dependencies and exception path.
Review adoption and evidence before expanding.
transfer_challenge.evidence: Two comparable weeks, a team-level record and one documented adoption decision.
transfer_challenge.review_after: At the end of the next week and before extending the rule to another team.

chapters.explanation: Productivity means completing results that serve an explicit purpose.
chapters.decision: Define the result first, then decide which activity deserves space.
actions: Write purpose and definition of done.
Remove one activity that changes no decision.
Name who approves the purpose and who reviews evidence.
chapters.rule: No task becomes a priority without a result and evidence. Respect rights, sensitive data and shared commitments.
chapters.example: Synthetic team example: Replace “answer email” with “resolve the three decisions blocking delivery”.
chapters.antipattern: Using task count as proof of productivity.
chapters.expected_evidence: A defensible priority decision. It is available for the agreed review.
chapters.limit: Necessary maintenance may remain; its cost must stay visible. Do not scale without reviewing dependencies and adoption.

chapters.explanation: A time log reduces dependence on vague recollection of the week.
chapters.decision: Record facts for a sufficient period before redesigning.
actions: Assign the record custodian and minimum read rights.
chapters.rule: A conclusion requires an inspectable record. Respect rights, sensitive data and shared commitments.
chapters.example: Synthetic team example: Record “10:00–10:35, meeting, output: date agreed”.
chapters.antipattern: Backfilling the log to confirm a prior impression.
chapters.expected_evidence: Traceable time log. It is available for the agreed review.
chapters.limit: The log describes the observed period, not a universal rule. Do not scale without reviewing dependencies and adoption.

chapters.explanation: The value map separates creation, support, coordination and reaction.
chapters.decision: Keep necessary work and question work that supports no result.
actions: Total time only to describe, not promise impact.
Agree with affected areas how ambiguous cases will be resolved.
chapters.rule: A category without a reason remains provisional. Respect rights, sensitive data and shared commitments.
chapters.example: Synthetic team example: Coordinating access is necessary support when it enables delivery.
chapters.antipattern: Calling necessary but less visible obligations “noise”.
chapters.expected_evidence: Reviewable value map. It is available for the agreed review.
chapters.limit: Classification depends on purpose and may change with context. Do not scale without reviewing dependencies and adoption.

chapters.explanation: The matrix exposes impact, real urgency, effort, dependency and risk.
chapters.decision: Rank results with the same criteria and explain the trade-off.
actions: Document the decision owner and dependency that may change it.
chapters.rule: Scoring informs; the accountable person decides. Respect rights, sensitive data and shared commitments.
chapters.example: Synthetic team example: Two results tie: choose the one that clears a critical dependency.
chapters.antipattern: Adding scores without explaining meaning or uncertainty.
chapters.expected_evidence: Three justified priorities. It is available for the agreed review.
chapters.limit: A matrix does not replace judgment, rights or existing commitments. Do not scale without reviewing dependencies and adoption.

chapters.explanation: A work limit exposes what is active and what is waiting.
chapters.decision: Finish, pause or remove before opening another front.
actions: Publish the active limit and who authorizes an exception.
chapters.rule: Every active front has a next action or is paused. Respect rights, sensitive data and shared commitments.
chapters.example: Synthetic team example: Keep three weekly results active and an explicit queue.
chapters.antipattern: Treating every request as started work.
checklist: Active limit and exception authority published.
chapters.expected_evidence: Fewer simultaneous fronts with clear status. It is available for the agreed review.
chapters.limit: The appropriate limit is contextual; no automatic outcome is promised. Do not scale without reviewing dependencies and adoption.

chapters.explanation: A protected block links priority, time and a concrete output.
chapters.decision: Schedule only when inputs and a definition of done exist.
actions: Confirm inputs, block owner and output reviewer.
chapters.rule: Redesign a block with no output before it starts. Respect rights, sensitive data and shared commitments.
chapters.example: Synthetic team example: 09:00–10:30, produce a reviewable draft with five sources ready.
chapters.antipattern: Filling the calendar without coordination or contingency capacity.
checklist: Inputs ready and output acceptance defined.
chapters.expected_evidence: Executable block. It is available for the agreed review.
chapters.limit: A legitimate, documented exception may reschedule a block. Do not scale without reviewing dependencies and adoption.

chapters.explanation: The protocol avoids deciding every interruption from scratch.
chapters.decision: Choose what to handle, delegate, batch, defer or discard.
actions: Assign each channel an owner and escalation path.
chapters.rule: Every exception records reason and next decision. Respect rights, sensitive data and shared commitments.
chapters.example: Synthetic team example: Non-urgent messages are batched; critical incidents use the agreed channel.
chapters.antipattern: Blocking requests without a valid urgency path.
chapters.expected_evidence: Focus protection rules. It is available for the agreed review.
chapters.limit: The protocol does not remove surprises or replace response to real risks. Do not scale without reviewing dependencies and adoption.

chapters.explanation: Weekly review connects results, deviations and adjustments.
chapters.decision: Keep one useful rule and change one friction per cycle.
actions: Give the review to the sponsor with an adoption decision.
chapters.rule: Keep an improvement only while its evidence remains visible. Respect rights, sensitive data and shared commitments.
chapters.example: Synthetic team example: Keep prior preparation; adjust message rule; review Friday.
chapters.antipattern: Turning review into blame or impressions.
checklist: Sponsor informed and adoption gate decided.
chapters.expected_evidence: Testable weekly rule. It is available for the agreed review.
chapters.limit: One period is insufficient to claim general improvement. Do not scale without reviewing dependencies and adoption.

chapters.explanation: The board combines priorities, blocks, status, evidence and next action.
chapters.decision: Show only information that changes a decision.
actions: Configure board access by role and need.
chapters.rule: The board must be understandable without reconstructing conversations. Respect rights, sensitive data and shared commitments.
chapters.example: Synthetic team example: Priority A: active; evidence: draft; next: review Thursday.
chapters.antipattern: Building an ornamental board that costs more upkeep than the work.
chapters.expected_evidence: Visible weekly system. It is available for the agreed review.
chapters.limit: Visibility must respect sensitive data and access rights. Do not scale without reviewing dependencies and adoption.

glossary.definition: Observable change or delivery with a definition of done.
Result chosen over explicit alternatives.
Reserved time with purpose, output and boundary.
External condition or contribution needed to continue.
Observable record used to review a claim.

faq.question: Always three priorities?
faq.answer: It is a practice limit that forces comparison; adjust it when context requires and document why. The sponsor documents any change to the limit.

faq.question: What about a real urgency?
faq.answer: Use the defined exception, record its evidence and explicitly reschedule or remove work. The exception authority records the decision.

faq.question: How do I know it improved?
faq.answer: Compare equivalent records and decide on one rule; do not turn one week into a general promise. The review team decides before scaling.

faq.question: May I share the board?
faq.answer: Only with the rights and detail level agreed for the people involved. Permissions determine which detail may be shared.

closing_checklist: Priorities, owners and reviewers are visible.
Dependencies and rights were reviewed.
Exceptions and backup ownership are defined.
Adoption is reviewed before scaling.

graph_summary.title: From diagnosis to review
graph_summary.body: The prompts turn authorized records into decisions with owner, reviewer, dependencies, rights and an adoption gate.
graph_summary.independent_use: Each prompt can run alone when you provide its declared input artifact; it never invents a prior output.

items.purpose: Turn scattered records into a factual map of the week. Produce a baseline the team can audit.
items.when: When you need a baseline before changing the calendar. Confirm the authorized period and record custodian.
workflow: Gather available calendar, task and note records.
Order activities by day, duration and output.
Summarize patterns as observations, not causes.
Close with record custodian, permissions and diagnosis reviewer.
guardrails: Do not invent periods or outputs.
Declare any reconstruction from memory.
Do not combine calendars without their owners’ permission.
acceptance_criteria: Every block has a source or a marker.
The summary separates facts from inference.
At least one relevant gap is identified.
The diagnosis has a documented custodian, reviewer and permissions.
edge_cases: Incomplete records: deliver a partial map.
Overlapping activities: keep both and mark conflict.
items.tradeoff: More detail improves traceability but increases recording effort. Governance adds coordination but reduces opaque decisions.
items.demo_artifact: Team Monday-to-Friday record: 96 h across four people; 31 h of meetings, 28 h of production, 17 h of coordination, 12 h of support, and 8 h unclassified. The client proposal is due Friday; five meetings have no recorded decision, and six interruptions have no owner.
limits: Describe the observed period; do not predict performance.
It does not authorize access, change or automatic adoption.

items.purpose: Classify activities by their relationship to value. Leave disputed categories ready for resolution.
items.when: When the time map exists and you must decide what to question. Confirm shared purpose and affected areas.
workflow: Read the period purpose and results.
Classify creation, maintenance, coordination or reaction.
Close with category ownership and a dispute resolution path.
guardrails: Do not trivialize necessary maintenance.
Do not assign value without a stated purpose.
Do not label another area’s work without its review.
acceptance_criteria: Every activity has a category and reason.
Uncertain cases preserve missing evidence.
The map supports keep, reduce or review decisions.
Categories have owners and a defined dispute path.
edge_cases: One activity serves two categories: record primary and secondary.
Without owner or rights, return a block and next gate.
items.tradeoff: A simple taxonomy aids decisions but loses nuance; preserve exceptions. Governance adds coordination but reduces opaque decisions.
items.demo_artifact: Team factual map: proposal 22 h and draft with six of ten sections complete; meetings 31 h and seven decisions; support 12 h and nine cases; coordination 17 h; 8 h unrecorded. Agreed outcome: proposal reviewed by Sales and Operations on Thursday.
limits: Classification is contextual, not universal.
It does not authorize access, change or automatic adoption.

items.purpose: Choose three results and expose trade-offs. Turn alternatives into explicit commitments.
items.when: When candidate results exceed available capacity. Confirm sponsor and available capacity.
workflow: Compare purpose, impact and real urgency.
Close with result owners and a sponsor for trade-offs.
guardrails: Do not use pressure as the only criterion.
Expose data that could change the order.
Do not assign priorities without a sponsor and confirmed capacity.
acceptance_criteria: Three observable results.
Each has a rationale and trade-off.
No hidden tie remains.
Every priority has an owner, sponsor and confirmed capacity.
edge_cases: Everything seems urgent: request evidence of date and consequence.
Capacity is missing: reduce scope before adding priority.
items.tradeoff: A limit of three creates clarity but defers legitimate work. Governance adds coordination but reduces opaque decisions.
items.demo_artifact: Team classification: proposal = creation; scope committee = coordination; daily report = maintenance; unchanneled requests = reaction. Three meetings produced no decision. Candidate outcomes: approved proposal, capacity decision, and validation of source rights.
limits: It does not guarantee completion; it creates a reviewable decision.
It does not authorize access, change or automatic adoption.

items.purpose: Test priorities against dependencies, effort, risk and calendar reality. Expose blocks before committing shared capacity.
items.when: Before reserving blocks or committing a date. Confirm who can resolve each dependency.
workflow: Compare effort with declared available space.
Close with validated dependencies and escalation ownership.
guardrails: Do not invent availability or agreements.
Separate internal from external dependency.
Do not mark a dependency resolved without owner validation.
acceptance_criteria: Every risk has a signal and response.
Dependencies have status.
The final decision explains the trade-off.
Every dependency has status, owner and next gate.
edge_cases: Dependency has no owner: mark blocked.
Risk lacks evidence: treat as hypothesis.
items.tradeoff: More validation reduces surprise but consumes time before execution. Governance adds coordination but reduces opaque decisions.
items.demo_artifact: Three prioritized outcomes: proposal approved Thursday, capacity confirmed Friday, and source rights resolved Wednesday. Shared capacity: 26 h. Accountable owner: sales lead. Independent reviewer: Operations. Supplier dependency unconfirmed; committee available Thursday at 15:00.
limits: This is a reality test, not certainty about the future.
It does not authorize access, change or automatic adoption.

items.purpose: Turn priorities into blocks with output and boundary. Deliver a calendar that can coordinate with other areas.
items.when: When priorities have passed the reality test. Confirm fixed commitments and output reviewers.
workflow: Assign blocks using declared work and available energy.
Define input, output and definition of done.
Close with block owners and reviewers for each output.
guardrails: Do not fill all capacity.
Do not move fixed commitments without authorization.
Do not move shared commitments without the relevant authority.
acceptance_criteria: Every priority has a block.
Every block has an output.
Conflicts are marked.
Every block has an owner, reviewer and agreed output.
edge_cases: No block is large enough: split the output.
Dependency pending: schedule preparation, not execution.
items.tradeoff: Long blocks reduce switching but reduce flexibility for exceptions. Governance adds coordination but reduces opaque decisions.
items.demo_artifact: Team reality test: keep proposal scope v1; reduce the capacity memo to one page; defer dashboard polish. Inputs: 8 h; integration: 6 h; review: 3 h. Risk: committee schedule. Mitigation: pre-read Wednesday at noon. Accountable owner: sales lead.
limits: The calendar is an executable hypothesis and must be reviewed.
It does not authorize access, change or automatic adoption.

items.purpose: Define default responses for interruptions. Produce response rules that respect critical channels. Run the protocol for one controlled week; prompt-07 will review its log and exceptions.
items.when: When messages and requests repeatedly displace blocks. Confirm critical channels and exception authority.
workflow: Assign handle, delegate, batch, defer or discard.
Close with channel owners and exception authority.
guardrails: Include a path for real urgency.
Do not block care, safety or critical service duties.
Do not block a critical channel without an agreed escalation path.
acceptance_criteria: Every type has response and timing.
Exceptions are explicit.
Language protects work without hostility.
Every interruption has a channel, owner and valid exception.
edge_cases: Ambiguous request: ask for consequence and date.
Authority conflict: escalate instead of improvising.
items.tradeoff: A rule protects focus but can delay coordination without exceptions. Governance adds coordination but reduces opaque decisions.
items.demo_artifact: Team blocks: Tuesday 09:00–11:00 architecture; Wednesday 09:00–12:00 drafting; Thursday 10:00–11:00 quality control; Thursday 15:00–16:00 committee; Friday 09:00–10:00 decision. Two hours remain unassigned as reserve. Conflict: critical support Wednesday at 10:00. Replanning owner: PM.
limits: Adapt the protocol to context and review its effects.
It does not authorize access, change or automatic adoption.

items.purpose: Compare plan, execution and evidence to choose one adjustment. Turn weekly evidence into a continuation decision. Source consultation is a conditional branch: activate prompt-08 only if review leaves a decision requiring governed external evidence.
items.when: At period close or before planning the next week. Confirm which practice week will be reviewed. The sequence may end here.
workflow: Identify one useful rule and one friction.
Propose an adjustment and review date.
Close with sponsor, evidence and the rule’s adoption gate.
guardrails: Do not turn perceived effort into evidence.
Do not generalize from one period.
Do not scale the rule before reviewing evidence and adoption.
acceptance_criteria: Facts and inferences are separate.
Each adjustment addresses a friction.
A keep-or-remove criterion exists.
The rule has a sponsor, evidence and adoption criterion.
edge_cases: Insufficient evidence: preserve the question; do not invent a conclusion.
Without owner or rights, return a block and next gate.
items.tradeoff: Testing one rule slows the pace of change but makes the evidence easier to connect to that adjustment. Governance adds coordination but reduces opaque decisions. Consulting sources adds traceability but is not required when local evidence is enough to close the decision.
items.demo_artifact: Team protocol applied: requests through one channel; reviews at 11:30 and 16:00; urgent only for safety, a blocked client, or a deadline under 4 h. Log: 24 interruptions, 13 queued, 6 handled, 3 delegated, and 2 escalated. The proposal reached committee; one critical case exceeded its SLA.
limits: Review supports decisions; it does not prove general improvement.
It does not authorize access, change or automatic adoption.

items.purpose: Build a cited synthesis for one concrete decision. Deliver a cited, reviewable recommendation.
items.when: In NotebookLM Sources, when a priority depends on governed information. Confirm source rights and the pending decision.
guardrails: Stop when relevant sources are absent.
Do not present editorial synthesis as observed fact.
Do not cite or distribute sources without verifiable rights.
acceptance_criteria: Every verifiable claim has a citation.
Disagreements remain visible.
The recommendation states its limit.
The recommendation preserves citations, rights and accountable reviewer.
edge_cases: Sources conflict: do not force consensus.
Unclear rights: exclude the source and record the gap.
items.tradeoff: Citations improve traceability but may leave an immediate decision unanswered. Governance adds coordination but reduces opaque decisions.
items.demo_artifact: Team review: proposal completed, capacity partly approved, and one source's rights pending. Adjustment: protect Wednesday's integration block. Open decision: evaluate the pilot by cycle time or quality. Available sources: brief v2, work log, committee minutes, and official guide; none establishes causality.
limits: Use only governed sources available in the notebook.
It does not authorize access, change or automatic adoption.

phases.label: Diagnosticar
phases.purpose: Ler sua semana sem confundir atividade com avanço.

phases.label: Desenhar
phases.purpose: Escolher resultados e reservar espaço real.

phases.label: Sustentar
phases.purpose: Proteger, revisar e transferir uma regra útil.

moments.explanation: Atividade descreve movimento; avanço exige um resultado útil e concluído. Aplique a um resultado próprio que possa verificar.
key_points: Nomeie o resultado antes de listar tarefas.
Use evidência observável para reconhecer avanço.
moments.application: Pegue uma tarefa recente e reescreva-a como resultado verificável.
moments.check_question: Que fato provaria que você avançou? Nomeie sua condição de concluído.
moments.micro_practice: Reescreva uma atividade como resultado, ação e evidência.
moments.takeaway: Estar ocupado não equivale a avançar.
moments.handoff: Leve o resultado ao diagnóstico de interrupções.

moments.explanation: Reagir sem regra fragmenta a semana e desloca resultados escolhidos. Observe qual reação própria você pode mudar.
key_points: Separe urgência real de pressão percebida.
Registre cada mudança de contexto antes de explicá-la.
moments.application: Revise duas interrupções e classifique-as como atender, agrupar, delegar ou adiar.
moments.check_question: Qual interrupção mudou uma prioridade justificada? Separe pressão externa de sua resposta.
moments.micro_practice: Defina uma resposta padrão para uma interrupção recorrente.
moments.takeaway: A reação precisa de regra, não de culpa.
moments.handoff: Use o registro para reconhecer trabalho que cria valor.

moments.explanation: O volume de tarefas não mostra valor; o resultado deve servir a um propósito declarado. Classifique a partir do propósito escolhido para sua semana.
key_points: Separe criação de valor, manutenção, coordenação e ruído.
Não elimine manutenção necessária: torne seu custo visível.
moments.application: Classifique cinco atividades recentes e justifique uma categoria duvidosa.
moments.check_question: Qual atividade consome tempo sem sustentar um resultado necessário? Marque a categoria que ainda gera dúvida.
moments.micro_practice: Coloque uma atividade ambígua no mapa e anote a evidência ausente.
moments.takeaway: O valor é argumentado; não presumido.
moments.handoff: Transforme o mapa em uma intenção semanal.

moments.explanation: Uma intenção concreta vem antes do esforço: defina o que deve mudar e para quem. Formule uma intenção compatível com seus limites reais.
key_points: Formule um resultado com condição de concluído.
Declare o limite que evita ampliar o trabalho sem controle.
moments.application: Complete: “Ao fim da semana ___ estará pronto, comprovado por ___”.
moments.check_question: A formulação ajuda a decidir o que fica de fora? Declare o limite que não negociará.
moments.micro_practice: Escreva uma prioridade em uma frase e elimine verbos vagos.
moments.takeaway: Primeiro direção; depois intensidade.
moments.handoff: Compare a intenção com o mapa real da semana.

moments.explanation: Um mapa da semana transforma lembranças dispersas em registro revisável. Use apenas registros pessoais que possa revisar.
key_points: Inclua reuniões, tarefas, blocos e mudanças de contexto.
Descreva fatos antes de julgá-los.
moments.application: Reconstrua um dia em blocos e marque o resultado de cada um.
moments.check_question: Qual período não pode ser explicado com evidência suficiente? Reconheça qualquer lacuna no registro.
moments.micro_practice: Complete manhã, tarde e fechamento de um dia real.
moments.takeaway: Observar vem antes de redesenhar.
moments.handoff: Use o mapa para selecionar apenas três prioridades.

moments.explanation: Três prioridades obrigam a comparar resultados e tornam renúncias visíveis. Aceite explicitamente o trabalho que deixará para depois.
key_points: Justifique cada prioridade com propósito e evidência.
Registre o que será adiado e por quê.
moments.application: Ordene cinco resultados candidatos e mantenha apenas três.
moments.check_question: Qual prioridade mudaria diante de uma urgência comprovada? Torne visível sua principal renúncia.
moments.micro_practice: Escreva três prioridades e uma renúncia explícita para cada uma.
moments.takeaway: Priorizar também é decidir o que não fazer agora.
moments.handoff: Teste as três prioridades com critérios comuns.

moments.explanation: Uma matriz explícita reduz decisões baseadas apenas em pressão ou preferência. Decida qual incerteza pode assumir sem delegar seu julgamento.
key_points: Compare impacto, urgência real, esforço, dependência e risco.
Explique empates e dados ausentes.
moments.application: Pontue dois resultados com os mesmos critérios e declare o trade-off.
moments.check_question: Que fato ausente poderia inverter a ordem? Indique a incerteza que aceitará.
moments.micro_practice: Revise uma prioridade com cinco critérios e marque uma incerteza.
moments.takeaway: Critérios visíveis tornam a decisão revisável.
moments.handoff: Transforme a prioridade escolhida em bloco protegido.

moments.explanation: Uma prioridade sem tempo reservado perde para o trabalho imediato. Reserve tempo sem invadir compromissos pessoais não negociáveis.
key_points: Cada bloco precisa de propósito, saída e condição de concluído.
Reserve margem para coordenação e contingências reais.
moments.application: Desenhe um bloco de 45–90 minutos com entrada, saída e limite.
moments.check_question: O que deve estar pronto antes do início do bloco? Confirme que o bloco cabe na sua semana.
moments.micro_practice: Agende um bloco real e registre uma condição válida de cancelamento.
moments.takeaway: A agenda torna a prioridade executável.
moments.handoff: Defina como protegerá esse bloco.

moments.explanation: Proteger o foco exige respostas combinadas para interrupções previsíveis. Defina uma resposta que respeite suas responsabilidades reais.
key_points: Decida o que atender, delegar, agrupar, adiar ou descartar.
Torne explícitas as exceções legítimas.
moments.application: Escreva uma regra para mensagens, pedidos urgentes e mudanças de contexto.
moments.check_question: Quem pode ativar uma exceção e com qual evidência? Esclareça a exceção que atenderia.
moments.micro_practice: Ensaie uma resposta curta que proteja o bloco sem ignorar urgência real.
moments.takeaway: Um limite útil inclui uma via de exceção.
moments.handoff: Teste a regra por uma semana e registre o ocorrido.

moments.explanation: A revisão compara plano e fatos; não premia nem pune a sensação de esforço. Avalie sua decisão com fatos do período observado.
key_points: Registre resultados, blocos realizados e desvios.
Mantenha uma regra útil e mude uma fricção concreta.
moments.application: Compare uma prioridade planejada com sua evidência e escolha manter, ajustar ou retirar.
moments.check_question: A explicação usa fatos ou uma história conveniente? Separe o fato da sua interpretação.
moments.micro_practice: Escreva um aprendizado, uma decisão e a evidência que sustenta ambos.
moments.takeaway: Revisar transforma experiência em regra testável.
moments.handoff: Integre os achados em um quadro visível.

moments.explanation: O sistema semanal reúne decisões e evidências em uma vista para agir e revisar. Mantenha apenas informação que ajude a decidir.
key_points: Mostre prioridades, blocos, estado e próxima decisão.
Mantenha o sistema pequeno e atualizado.
moments.application: Crie uma vista de uma página com três prioridades e a próxima evidência.
moments.check_question: É possível entender o estado sem reconstruir conversas? Escolha a próxima decisão que mostrará.
moments.micro_practice: Remova um campo que não muda decisões e acrescente o fato ausente.
